<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par91 />defective writing is especially frequent in the ''3rd masc. sing.'' {{GHGheb|text=־ָו}}, which in {{GHGterm|Q<sup>e</sup>rê}} is almost always changed to {{GHGheb|text=־ָיו}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=חִצָּו|translate=his arrows}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=58|verse=8}}, {{GHGterm|Q<sup>e</sup>rê}} {{GHGheb|text=חִצָּיו}}. On {{GHGheb|text=יַחְדָּו}}, only three times {{GHGheb|text=יַחְדָּיו}}, cf. {{GHGpar|135|r}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|91|l}}
2. Unusual forms (but for the most part probably only scribal errors) are—''Sing.'' 2nd pers. ''fem'' {{GHGheb|text=־ֵיךְ}} (after {{GHGheb|text=אַשְׁרֵי|translate=happy!}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=10|verse=17}}, which has become stereotyped as an interjection, and is therefore unchangeable; cf. Delitzsch on the passage); {{GHGheb|text=־ַ֫ יְכִי}} (cf. Syr. {{GHGheb|text=־ֵכִי}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=4|verse=3}}, and <sup>7</sup> in {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>th.}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=103|verse=3–5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=116|verse=7|hidebook=1}} ({{GHGheb|text=־ָ֫ יְכִי}} in {{GHGterm|pause}}).—In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=16|verse=31}} {{GHGheb|text=־ַ֫ יִךְ}} (so {{GHGheb|text=־ֵיכֶם}} in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=6|verse=8|hidebook=1}}) occurs with an ''infin.'' ending in {{GHGheb|text=וֹת}}, the {{GHGheb|text=וֹת}} being therefore treated as a plural ending; similarly, the plural suffix is sometimes found with the feminine ending {{GHGheb|text=וּת}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=14|verse=33}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=54|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=3|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=16|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=23|verse=7|hidebook=1}}, as well as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=16|verse=20|hidebook=1}} {{GHGterm|Q<sup>e</sup>rê}}, and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zp|chapter=3|verse=20}}), with the ending ''îth'' ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=5|verse=24}}, reading {{GHGheb|text=חֲמִֽשִׁתוֹ}}), and even with the ordinary feminine ending ''ath''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=47|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=35|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=9|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ezr|chapter=9|verse=15}}.—Wholly abnormal is {{GHGheb|text=מַלְאָכֵ֫כֵה|translate=thy messengers}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Na|chapter=2|verse=14}}, evidently a case of dittography of the following {{GHGheb|text=ה}}: read {{GHGheb|text=מַלְאָכַ֫יִךְ}}.

''3rd masc.'' {{GHGheb|text=־ֵ֫ יהוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Hb|chapter=3|verse=10}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=24|verse=23}}; {{GHGheb|text=־ֵ֫ הוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=30|verse=26}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=43|verse=17}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Na|chapter=2|verse=4}}; {{GHGheb|text=וֹ֫הִי}} (a purely Aramaic form) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=116|verse=12}}.—''3rd fem.'' {{GHGheb|text=־ֶ֫ יהָא}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=41|verse=15}}.

''Plur.'' The strange ''2nd pers. masc.'' {{GHGheb|text=תְּפוֹצֽוֹתִיכֶם}} (with ''î'', so Qimḥi; cf. Norzi) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=25|verse=34}}, is probably a mixed form combining {{GHGheb|text=תָּפ֫וּצוּ}} and {{GHGheb|text=הֲפִיצֽוֹתִיכֶם}}; {{GHGterm|fem.}} {{GHGheb|text=־ֵיכֶ֫נָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=13|verse=20}}.

''3rd masc.'' {{GHGheb|text=־ֵיהֵ֫מָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=40|verse=16}}; {{GHGterm|fem.}} {{GHGheb|text=־ֵיהֶ֫נָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=1|verse=11}}.

3. The termination {{GHGheb|text=־ֵ֫מוֹ}} (also with the ''dual'', e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=58|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=59|verse=13|hidebook=1}}), like {{GHGheb|text=מוֹ}} and {{GHGheb|text=־ָ֫ מוֹ}}, occurs with the noun (as with the verb, {{GHGpar|58|g}}) almost exclusively in the later poets [viz. with a substantive in the singular, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=21|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=17|verse=10.10|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=58|verse=7|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=59|verse=13|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=89|verse=18|hidebook=1}}; with a dual or plural, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=32|verse=27.32.37.38}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=33|verse=29|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=2|verse=3.3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=11|verse=7|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=35|verse=16|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=49|verse=12|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=58|verse=7|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=59|verse=14|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=73|verse=5.7|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=83|verse=12.12|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=140|verse=4.10|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=27|verse=23}}; after prepositions, see {{GHGpar|103|f}}, o, notes], and cannot, therefore, by itself be taken as an indication of archaic language. On the other hand there can be no doubt that these are revivals of really old forms. That they are consciously and artificially used is shown by the evidently intentional accumulation of them, e.g. in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=15|verse=5.7.9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=2|verse=3.5}}, and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=140|verse=4.10|hidebook=1}}, and also by the fact observed by Diehl (see the heading of this section) that in Ex 15 they occur ''only'' as verbal suffixes, in Dt 32 ''only'' as noun suffixes.

{{GHGmargin-letter|91|m}}
'''3.''' It is clear and beyond doubt that the {{GHGterm|Yôdh}} in these suffixes with the plural noun belongs, in reality, to the ending of the {{GHGterm|construct state}} of the masculine plural. Yet the consciousness of this fact became so completely lost as to admit of the striking peculiarity (or rather inaccuracy) of appending those ''suffix''-forms which include the plural ending {{GHGheb|text=־ֵי}}, even to the feminine plural in {{GHGheb|text=וֹת}} ({{GHGheb|text=סֽוּסוֹתֵ֫ינוּ}}, {{GHGheb|text=סֽוּסוֹתֶ֫יךָ}}, &c.), so that in reality the result is a double indication of the plural.<ref>See an analogous case in {{GHGpar|87|s}}. Cf. also the double feminine ending in the ''3rd sing. perf.'' of verbs {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}}, {{GHGpar|75|i}}.</ref>

{{GHGmargin-letter|91|n}}
Such is the rule: the singular suffix, however (see b), also occurs with the ending {{GHGheb|text=וֹת}} (probably through the influence of Aramaic), e.g. {{GHGheb|text=עֵֽדְוֹתִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=132|verse=12}} (unless it be ''sing.'' for {{GHGheb|text=עֵֽדוּתִי}}, as, according to Qimḥi in his Lexicon, {{GHGheb|text=תַּֽחֲנֹתִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=6|verse=8}} is for {{GHGheb|text=תַּֽחֲנוּתִי}}); {{GHGheb|text=מַכֹּֽתְךָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=28|verse=59}} (treated on the analogy of an ''infin.'' {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}});<section end=par91 /><noinclude>
